sourceObservations.observations: Title identifies Lecture 18 Manipulator–Mechanism Design-I, printed page 1, instructor and campus photo; no substantive concept.
Six outcome bullets including DOF, five robot configurations, performance, wrist/manipulability and Python workspace; blank lower-right presentation box, no hidden figure.
Five topic outline bullets, no new technical claims.
Diagram labels whole articulated arm Manipulator and circles only distal gripper End-Effector. Text relates physical design to performance and model complexity and lists four system parts.
Task-specific economic/practical design, heavy welding versus rapid board insertion, iterative joint arrangement and actuator/sensor decisions underlined red.

Three illustrated revolute joints theta1–theta3; DOF independent configuration variables, typical one per serial joint, Grübler named but not derived. Final else redundant statement overbroad: fewer DOF is not redundancy.
Six independent pose components and task-relative surplus DOF; axial tool symmetry removes required roll only if task is invariant to it.
Reachable work volume, scale/shape, singularity locations and structural intrusion. Blue 3-D point-cloud workspace with colored arm; illustrative, no recoverable quantitative point requirement.

Load definition throughout workspace versus explicitly configuration-dependent capacity; extended arm lower example; link sizing, gears/belts, torque/force, inertial and velocity loads. Need distinguish guaranteed worst-case rating from local maximum.
Peak speed versus cycle time; acceleration/deceleration emphasized for short pick-place; painting/welding process can impose rate.
Repeatability taught point versus accuracy mathematical point; 0.001 inch versus 8±2 inch spray example; link calibration and manufacturing tolerances.
Red ellipse marks first-three positioning joints, blue distal wrist; n−3 orienting joints, usually intersecting; simple twist angles0±90 and zero offsets, not universal guarantee.
Side view vertical d2 and horizontal d3; top view transverse d1. Three orthogonal P axes and hatched rectangular workspace. Singularity claim explicitly positioning only; stiffness gantry example.
Cartesian inverse direct displacements; linear-actuator speed and rigidity/payload; fixtures within support structure make retrofit restrictive, not every possible Cartesian installation.

Articulated shoulder yaw theta1 top view; shoulder elevation theta2 and parallel elbow theta3 side view. Hatched nearly spherical partial workspace, boundary and internal singularities, not exact full sphere.
Cantilevering reduces typical stiffness; compact support permits confined access; less structure for given volume and potentially more complex control/IK, all design trade-offs not absolute laws.

SCARA three parallel R plus P normal to plane; text calls P fourth while diagram labels vertical stroke d3. Three parallel red axes marked, top view theta1/theta2. Historical Adept One 1984 direct-drive and30ft/s plus rough10x claim are source attributions, not universal guarantees.

Base-mounted first-two actuators reduce moving mass; weight-support wording confuses zero vertical-axis gravity torque with nonzero bearing loads. Stiff Z/compliant XY; equal L1=L2 favors workspace and simpler IK, not universal optimality.

Spherical RRP: side elevation theta2, radial stroke d3, top azimuth theta1; hatched shell sectors. Retracted slider may protrude behind, requiring whole-mechanism clearance; symmetric-tool tasks mentioned.

Cylindrical text lists vertical P then vertical-axis R and radial P, while diagram labels yaw theta1, vertical d2 and radial d3. Independent cylindrical coordinates, material-handling use; do not universalize joint ordering.

Circled wrist theta4/5/6 after arm theta1/2/3. Conventional intersecting orthogonal wrist all orientations only without limits; this is not nonsingularity. Three-roll nonorthogonal continuous rotation depends on design.

Cross-section caption explicitly orthogonal-axis remote-actuator wrist using three concentric shafts A4/A5/A6, despite adjacent text continuing nonorthogonal excluded cone. Three-consecutive-intersecting-axes closed-form claim needs ordinary serial/nonredundant scope.

Actual displayed L=sum i=1..N of (a_(i−1)+d_i). Prismatic d_i is full stroke constant rather than instantaneous coordinate. Structural index requires consistent physical nonnegative length convention; signed DH sum caveat.

Actual Q_L=L/cuberoot(W); dimensionless and smaller structural length for same volume better. Cartesian minimum3 for equal travel under ideal sum model; articulated .62 only idealized workspace model, not universal superiority.

Displayed square det J=0 criterion and w=sqrt(det(JJ^T)), square simplification absdetJ. Rank loss means instantaneous task directions, not physical joints. Product of singular values is not conditioning ratio; same coordinate normalization is essential.

Displayed Mx=J^-T M J^-1 and X^T Mx X=1. Requires square invertible J; positive mass metric yields principal lengths inverse square roots. Right figure local ellipses vary size/orientation over annular sector; isotropy requires scalar identity in same units. Physical acceleration claim also requires force-limit assumptions.
Explicit l1=5,l2=4, both angles−pi..pi, correct fixed-frame FK x=l1cos(theta1)+l2cos(theta1+theta2), y analogous. No physical length-unit label supplied.
Illustrated serial2R labels l1,l2 and relative theta2 at elbow, theta1 at base; printed symbolic and substituted FK consistent.
Continuous radius1..9 from |l1−l2| and sum; actual plotted finite grid cannot contain every position although slide wording says all. r=sqrt(x²+y²).

Actual code imports numpy and pyplot;200 inclusive angles each; nested t1 outer and t2 inner append paired FK values; scatter s1, figsize8x8, equal axes. Title single-quoted text visually wraps to second line, syntactically invalid if literal newline copied; explicitly rejoin only title to execute.

Actual output scatter annulus hole radius1 outernear9, visible concentric/nonuniform dot rings, equal X/Y scale. Red arrows indicate inner/outer radius, not motion trajectory; finite sampling artifacts not obstacles.
Summary recaps task-dependent mechanism, stiffness/speed/control, structural/manipulability indices and Python FK workspace; no new independent equation.
Reference-only page, Craig Introduction to Robotics Mechanics and Control third edition2005; no substantive new teaching claim.
Thank-you closing page only.

independentAnswers.reasoning: Physical arrangement changes geometric transforms and inertial couplings, not just joint count.
The visible label calls the articulated structure the manipulator and circles the distal gripper as end-effector.
Heavy load and rapid small-part insertion demand different mechanical compromises even when both robots are programmable.
Three independent one-coordinate joints give three configuration variables; fixed base adds none.
Loop closure introduces coordinate dependencies; joint count alone omits those constraints.
A local rigid pose has three translation and three orientation coordinates, but actuation count does not guarantee reachable geometry.
Three positions plus two tool-axis directions specify five coordinates; irrelevant axial roll leaves one surplus freedom at full task rank.
Redundancy is surplus independent task freedom, not a shortage; a shortage can preclude a general target.
Equal volume does not preserve shape, conditioning or full-arm collision clearance.
A guarantee across both configurations cannot exceed min(12,7)=7kg; untested configurations could be worse.
Structure/transmission/actuator capability and configuration/dynamic effort all constrain payload; static weight or peak speed alone does not.
Short moves can remain acceleration-limited and never attain the common velocity cap.
The process fixes productive welding speed; excess robot capability need not change that part of the cycle.
A tight repeated cluster is repeatability; displacement from modeled target is absolute error.
Precision beyond process need adds cost without necessarily improving the wide spray result.
Estimating actual geometry aligns the inverse/forward model with manufactured links; it does not physically remove backlash.
The marked partition places the wrist center with first three joints and orients through n−3 distal joints.
Special twist angles, zero geometric parameters and intersecting wrist axes simplify transforms/decoupling; arbitrary skew or longer links do not guarantee it.
Three mutually orthogonal P translations sweep a box.
Actual side figure vertical arrow is d2, horizontal arrow d3; top displacement is d1.
Differentiating x=d1,y=d2,z=d3 gives I3, rank3 and determinant1 throughout the ideal interior.
Rigidity/payload benefit trades against surrounding support and fixture integration restrictions.
Elbow and shoulder-elevation axes are parallel in the pictured articulated architecture.
The hatched side/top sectors and text show a nearly spherical complex reach, not guaranteed isotropy or absence of internal singularities.
Cantilevered compact arms permit access but typically sacrifice stiffness and may need more complex IK/control.
Three parallel rotations provide planar positioning/yaw, with normal prismatic motion; do not infer numbering from contradictory prose.
The d3 arrow moves up and down normal to the horizontal links.
Four independent SCARA freedoms correspond to x,y,z and yaw away from singularities, not six arbitrary pose components.
The source explicitly attributes Adept One, direct drive,1984 and30ft/s; this is not independent historical/product verification.
Base mounting removes actuator mass from moving links, reducing moving inertia, not all payload inertia.
Text emphasizes vertical stiffness with planar compliance for insertion.
Gravity parallel to a vertical axis produces no moment component about that axis, yet bearing/link force remains.
Triangle inequality gives rmin=|L1−L2|; equal positive links cancel at full fold.
Spherical design retains two shoulder rotations and replaces elbow rotation with radial slide.
d3 is radial stroke; full slider geometry can protrude rearward on retraction.
Visible diagram theta1 is top-view yaw, d2 vertical and d3 radial.
Independent height, azimuth and radius match the cylindrical material-handling task.
Circled distal wrist contains theta4,theta5,theta6 only.
Unlimited joint travel is stated; orientation coverage does not eliminate rate singularities.
Continuous roll is compatible with an inaccessible cone for the third-axis direction.
Caption explicitly says orthogonal-axis wrist, remote actuators,three concentric shafts; surrounding paragraph is a different wrist discussion.
Source associates consecutive intersecting axes with closed form, with stated restriction against universalizing to arbitrary mechanisms.
Prismatic contribution is full travel, independent of current position.
Cube root8m³=2m;6m/2m=3 dimensionless.
With same positive W, QL is proportional to L; it says nothing alone about stiffness/payload/accuracy.
AM–GM gives u+v+w≥3(uvw)^(1/3), equality iff all positive travels equal.
Volumes both8; sums10 and6 give indices5 and3.
The0.62 is source-attributed ideal benchmark, not universal measured performance.
Jacobian rank loss removes instantaneous independent task velocities, not physical joints or FK existence.
JJT=diag(4,9), determinant36 and square root6; equivalently absdetJ=6.
JJT=diag(1,4),det4,w2,rank2; third input is null direction, not missing task row.
Both singular-value products1; A ratio100 versus B ratio1 distinguishes anisotropy.
Gram matrix JJT is singular exactly when task rows are linearly dependent.
Inertia metric adds mass distribution and configuration to kinematic Jacobian dependence.
Ordinary J inverse requires square nonsingular matrix; all matrices must share configuration/coordinate conventions.
J inverse diag(1/2,1) on both sides gives diag(8/4,3)=diag(2,3).
4u²+v²=1 gives intercepts|u|=.5 and|v|=1.
Scalar positive identity3I gives equal eigenvalues and circular normalized metric; other options anisotropic or non-PD.
Visible ellipses rotate/stretch across the region, representing configuration-dependent local inertia metrics.
Elbow theta2 is relative to link1, so fixed-frame link2 angle is theta1+theta2.
theta1+theta2=0; x=5cos(pi/2)+4=4,y=5sin(pi/2)+0=5.
Squaring FK yields25+16+40[cosθ1cos(θ1+θ2)+sinθ1sin(θ1+θ2)]=41+40cosθ2.
Full joint ranges permit exact fold radius1 and straight radius9.
Radius of(.6,.6)=sqrt(.72)<1; other radii1,9,5 lie in interval.
cosθ2 maximum1 at0 givesr9;minimum−1 at±pi givesr1.
Area π(9²−1²)=80π square units, not cubic volume for a3D structural index.
Finite grid maps40000 configurations; continuous joint domain maps infinitely many annular positions.
Ordinary single quotes cannot span a literal newline; parsing fails before loops execute.
Cartesian product200×200=40000 iterations; each appends one x and one y.
Outer t1 stays fixed while inner t2 traverses200 values.
zip pairs corresponding entries only, yielding200 configurations, not Cartesian product.
Inclusive−pi/+pi are physically same orientation; many-to-one FK further defeats uniqueness.
Set−pi+2pi k/199=0 implies k99.5, not integer; k99,100 give±pi/199.
r²=41+40cosθ2, maximized by smallest|θ2|=pi/199; result below9.
400²/200²=4, giving160000 pairs and FK evaluations.
axis equal enforces equal data scale; square figure alone does not fix axes data scaling.
Nonlinear FK maps uniform angular grid nonuniformly; code has no obstacles and no time dynamics.
Structural length is only one criterion; all specified task-performance and cell constraints still matter.
Source four-part list: manipulator,end-effector,external sensors/effectors,controller.
Symmetry may remove roll requirement but three positioning freedoms do not independently specify a general6Dpose.
Positive lengths mean det zero iff sinθ2=0; allowed zeros−pi,0,pi correspond folded/straight boundaries. Since determinant is already supplied, this is not a hard derivation item.
